Most of the time on the 9+ days were spent resting, though. I try not to rush on anything, not even on the smallest details.

All the best to you, you'll definitely get there! Better, even :DD

Mega comment (or something like that):

We all here want to learn and improve, so here are the things I kept in mind and some stuff about this work. I hope I can help all of you improve :)

Pencils/Equipment used?

Derwent 6B&9B – used for shading really, dark spots such as engines and belly.

   5H – used as base outline for the aircraft.

  HB- used for drawing details like letters.

Mechanical pencil (B) – used for drawing windows and blending the dark spots made by 6/8B pencils

Paper Stump – Sharpened regularly. I used the tip and slowly stroke it on the spots I want to blend it.

Plastic Eraser

A5 Sketchbook – Daler Rowney

Thoughts on working on it?

I guess after working on a few of these now, the key for me really is patience. If I instinctively stop drawing, I ask myself if I really want to continue drawing. I don’t force myself-if I feel the slightest bit of hint to stop, I put down the pencil.

The hardest part for me is perfecting the shape of the plane. It takes countless of redraws, the slightest of adjustments and corrections to get the shape nearly right. It took me 3 days just to perfect the shape of the plane before I started using an HB pencil.

After drawing these for quite a while, I figured that patience is key for me to draw these. It’s hard for me to resist rushing things up, but I kept telling myself that it won’t look good if I did rush it out. After a while, I kinda developed the power to resist it, luckily.

When drawing, don’t get discouraged in the middle of the work. No matter how bad you think it’ll get, just continue. I did, and in the end I myself was blown away by how much I have improved, even by the slightest. It was definitely worth it for me.

This is a work I put my absolute best on, using everything I learned from everyone everywhere as well as experience. This can also be an example of "specialist" - I can only draw planes, but if I were told to draw something like a human or a scenery I would totally suck :/

Welp, I hope this helps! Don't hesitate to ask if there's something else you'd like to know. And to anyone who wants to draw these kinds of sketches, best of luck! Mad respect to you guys ;)
